title: Self-Hosted CI/CD Pipeline
desc: From a Git push to a running website. A Linux-based deployment environment with a self-hosted runner, Docker, Nginx, and deployment verification.
problem: Create a repeatable path from source control to a self-hosted website without relying on manual file transfers.
solution: GitHub Actions assigns a workflow job to the Linux runner. The runner executes deployment tasks on the host; Docker and Nginx serve the static application.
steps: Prepare the Linux Mint host and Docker runtime.
Install the GitHub Actions runner as a service under a separate account.
Use the pardo-deploy runner label to target deployment jobs.
Deploy static application assets and verify the HTTP response.
results: The server serves the complete static website through a pinned Nginx container. Deployments validate release files and HTTP responses, with rollback on failed verification.
lesson: Treat runner permissions, host services, container workloads, and application health as separate concerns.

title: AWS High-Availability Architecture
desc: Exploring application availability through load balancing, Auto Scaling, and deliberate network design.
problem: Understand how an application can distribute traffic and recover capacity across multiple availability zones.
solution: The lab explores an Application Load Balancer in front of EC2 instances managed by an Auto Scaling Group, with VPC networking and security group boundaries.
steps: Define network boundaries and security groups.
Explore load balancer target health and scaling policies.
results: Presented as an educational AWS lab. No continuous production operation, availability percentage, or performance benchmark is claimed.
lesson: Availability depends on application health, network paths, and recovery behavior together.
future: Publish configuration evidence and diagrams from the lab.
Document failure scenarios and cost tradeoffs.

title: Serverless Task API
desc: An API-driven task application exploring event-driven architecture and managed AWS services.
problem: Explore a task API without managing application servers.
solution: API Gateway receives HTTP requests, Lambda handles application logic, and DynamoDB provides managed persistence. IAM defines service permissions.
steps: Connect API routes to Lambda handlers.
results: A project entry for the serverless task API. Public endpoints, test results, and a verified repository link have not been supplied.
lesson: Managed infrastructure still requires careful validation, permission scoping, and error handling.
future: Add reviewed API examples and repository links.
Publish verified response samples and validation results.

title: Infrastructure Monitoring
desc: Read-only Linux host measurements, Docker health checks, GitHub workflow history, and seven days of recorded host history.
problem: Make host and application behavior observable through a safe, read-only public interface.
solution: Unprivileged host collection and a separate fixed-query container collector publish sanitized snapshots. The browser cannot administer the host.
steps: Collect aggregate host counters every fifteen seconds.
Read website container health through a separate restricted collector.
Cache public GitHub deployment workflow runs.
Record one sample per minute with seven-day retention.
results: The local dashboard displays measured host and container data, workflow runs, and recorded history. Measurements do not establish internet availability.
lesson: Keep operational data separate from privileged administration and show unavailable or stale sources honestly.
future: Activate email delivery after sender configuration.
Add an independent monitor for complete server outages.
